subject: Post-demo: BrightCart performance targets & streaming plan
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightcart.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@brightcart.com>, BrightCart SRE <sre@brightcart.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick follow on demo — performance questions

Sean — thanks again for the demo earlier. Tom and our SRE team had a few follow-ups we want to lock down before moving forward:

1) Time-to-first-token (TTFT) expectations — we saw good end-to-end numbers in the demo but need concrete targets to include in our internal runbook. Our goal for checkout flows is a median TTFT of around 120–180ms and p95 under 450ms for typical cart sizes.

2) Streaming behavior — we’re planning progressive UI updates (order summary + upsell lines) that expect chunked responses. Can you confirm support for sub-200ms chunk cadence and whether Redwood recommends SSE vs WebSocket for browser clients (we have a mix of SPA and some legacy iframes).

3) Concurrency and throughput — initial rollout will target ~30 simultaneous inference sessions per region, bursting to 150 during peak promos. How should we size reserved capacity / burst capacity to avoid queuing?

Could you put together a short SLO table and a recommended config we can show our SREs? Attaching a spreadsheet with our traffic profile.

—Maria
Maria Lopez
Head of Product Engineering | BrightCart

Attachment: brightcart-traffic-sample.csv (see attached spreadsheet)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick follow on demo — performance questions

Hi Maria — great questions, thanks for the clarity. I pulled in Marissa (solutions) and Dev (runtime) to draft a concise, actionable plan. Summary below; attaching a compact SLO matrix and a sample playback we used in the demo.

High-level SLOs (proposed)
- Target median TTFT: 150ms (measured at edge for 95% of requests using our standard inference path)
- Target p95 TTFT: < 400ms (with reserved capacity; see notes on burst handling)
- Target steady-state chunk cadence: 120–220ms per chunk for ~300–600 token responses
- Preferred streaming transport: SSE for browser SPA friendliness and automatic reconnect semantics; WebSocket supported if you need multiplexed RPC and lower overhead for many small chunks.

Sizing/throughput guidance
- Initial reserved capacity: configure for sustained 40 concurrent streams per region to leave headroom vs your 30 target.
- Burst policy: enable burst capacity up to 180 concurrent for promo windows; auto-fallback to smaller model variant if capacity exceeded.
- Token throughput estimate: estimate 15–25 requests/sec per GPU for your prompt sizes; we’ll map exact numbers after playback traces.

Engineering notes (Dev)
- Use prefix/KV cache for repeated cart templates to reduce TTFT on common requests.
- Continuous batching should be set to low-latency mode (max batch delay 6–8ms) given your TTFT targets.
- Chunk framing: recommend 256-token chunk windows with client-side buffer to render on first chunk.

Action items
1) Redwood: Marissa to share trimmed SLO matrix + recommended Dedicated config (attached).
2) BrightCart: share peak-day playback trace (we’ll replay against staging).
3) Schedule a 60-min SRE sync next week to validate queuing behavior under promo traffic.

I’ve attached the SLO matrix (brightcart-slo-matrix.xlsx) and a short playback sample (redwood-playback-sample.json). If that looks good I can loop in Account Engineering for dedicated sizing and a short two-hour load run.

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: RE: internal: BrightCart sizing recommendations

Internal notes for the sync — leaving these here so we have a single record before the SRE call.

Observations from demo traces:
- Demo playback showed median TTFT ~130ms when running on a 40-token warm prompt with prefix cache warm. Cold prompts jumped to ~340ms.
- Chunk cadence averaged ~180ms with SSE in our test harness (client-side simulated render latency small).

Recommendations to minimize risk:
- For BrightCart profile, recommend Dedicated pool with 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs per region for initial rollout (allows sustained throughput and lowers p95).
- Set continuous batching max_delay to 6ms and max_batch_size tuned to your observed concurrency (start at 64).
- Turn on prefix caching for product templates; this drops median TTFT by ~30–50ms in our measurements.
- If they need sub-100ms median TTFT consistently, we’ll need per-customer edge caching plus smaller prompt engineering and possibly a smaller param model tuned for latency.

Prep for SRE call:
- I’ll bring sample JMX-style load plan and the playback script.
- Marissa — can you prepare a one-slide SLO summary and the Dedicated config options?

—Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Runtime Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: sla-draft-brightcart.pdf

Subject: Re: Post-demo: BrightCart performance targets & streaming plan

Thanks — this is very helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few quick clarifications before the SRE call: 

- SSE vs WebSocket: we prefer SSE unless WebSocket gives a measurable improvement in p95; can you include both transport latency numbers from your playback?
- Chunk cadence tolerance: our frontend team requests that the first chunk arrive within 200ms for acceptable UX. Can you confirm the plan to get first chunk under 200ms in 95% of cases?
- Failure modes: please include expected behavior under queueing (e.g., 503 vs delayed chunk stream) so our UX can handle graceful degradation.

If you can add these notes into the SLO slide and attach a short failure-mode table, we’ll be ready to sign off on a two-week staging test. Also we’ll route the DocuSign link to procurement after the staging run.

Next steps agreed: 1) Redwood updates SLO slide with transport numbers + failure modes, 2) BrightCart provides peak-day trace, 3) SRE sync: Thu 12/10 at 11am PT.

—Maria
